summary: A DataScientest blog article (February 2, 2024) comparing Python and Julia for data science and machine learning. It describes Julia's strengths (created for data science, REPL, JIT compilation via LLVM, speed comparable to C, mathematical syntax, automatic memory management) and Python's advantages (lighter runtime, faster startup, improving interpreter, larger community and third-party packages like PyTorch and TensorFlow). The conclusion is that Julia can outperform Python in speed and ease of use for these disciplines, but Python remains an excellent choice given its community.
one_line: A blog comparison of Python and Julia for data science and machine learning, weighing Julia's speed and design against Python's popularity and package ecosystem.
key_facts: Python was introduced in the 1990s and remains one of the world's most popular programming languages.
More than 7 million coders use Python, according to the article.
Julia was created in 2012 as a newer language for data science and machine learning.
Julia's creators aimed to offer Python-like usability with the computational capabilities of Matlab and the speed of C.
A 2020 user survey conducted by Julia developers among 2565 users found that 76% of Julia users would choose Python as their second language.
Julia uses the LLVM framework for just-in-time (JIT) compilation, enabling it to offer the same runtime speed as C.
Julia provides an interactive REPL (Read Eval Print Loop) command line.
Julia is compatible with a wide variety of external Python, Fortran and C libraries.
Julia's syntax is optimized for mathematics and resembles the formulas mathematicians use, similar to R, Octave, Matlab and Mathematica.
Julia features automatic memory management and supports metaprogramming, letting programs generate other Julia applications.
Python's runtime is lighter than Julia's and Python programs generally take less time to start running.
Python's interpreter has improved, particularly for parallel and multi-core processing.
Python benefits from third-party packages such as PyTorch and Tensorflow for Machine Learning, while very little third-party software is being developed around Julia.
The article concludes Julia can outperform Python in speed and ease of use for data science and machine learning, but Python remains an excellent choice.
